evals.prompt: I'm interviewing a former restaurant owner for a feature on why small kitchens close. She asked to keep part of it 'off the record'. How should I handle that and write it up?
evals.expected_output: Should first read the publication's writing guide and profile (the folder AGENTS.md or the user's personal agent instructions name, else the project's publications/; in a chat app, the project's files; else ask). Should agree the ground rules in plain words before the interview, because not everyone understands 'off the record' or 'on background' the same way: say what each means here — not published at all, or usable without her name. Should agree how she'll be identified, keep a dated record of the terms, and never publish anything agreed off the record. Anonymity is the exception and its reason is told to readers. The terms go in the topic folder's interviews/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<name>.md, filled from the interview notes template, with consent for name, quote and recording recorded at the top. Should read the topic's brief.md before asking, asking only what it leaves open (such as whether she may see a draft, from the writing guide's policy).
expectations: Reads the publication's guide and profile first
Reads brief.md before asking and asks only what it and the guide leave open
Agrees what 'off the record' means in plain words before the interview
Agrees how the source will be identified
Records the agreed terms with dates in interviews/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<name>.md in the topic folder, from the notes template
Never publishes material agreed as off the record

evals.prompt: The founder I'm profiling says he'll only do the interview if we pay him $500 for his time. Our budget can cover it — fine to go ahead?
evals.expected_output: Should advise against it: the SPJ code, revised in October 2026, says do not pay sources in exchange for interviews or information. Should suggest alternatives such as a shorter call, written answers attributed as 'said in an email', or other sources, and note that a commissioned contributor's fee for writing is a different arrangement the publication's policy governs. Should not present payment as acceptable because the budget allows it.
expectations: Advises against paying the source for the interview
Cites the SPJ code's rule on paying sources
Offers alternatives such as written answers or other sources
Distinguishes a contributor's writing fee from paying for information

evals.prompt: From two separate parts of my interview transcript I have: 'Prices went up every month' and, later, 'we lost half our regulars that year'. Can I join them into one quote: 'Prices went up every month and we lost half our regulars that year'?
evals.expected_output: Should say no: never stitch remarks from different moments into one quote, and never distort facts or context. Should offer to quote each line separately with attribution, or to paraphrase the connection in the writer's own words. Should also check both lines against the audio before quoting, because automatic transcripts mishear names, numbers and terms.
expectations: Refuses to combine remarks from different moments into one quote
Offers separate quotes or a paraphrase instead
Checks the transcript against the audio before quoting

evals.prompt: Send my questions to a retired fire chief for a piece on wildfire preparedness — I'll quote whatever he emails back.
evals.expected_output: Should note that written answers come back polished and can't be followed up in the moment; prefer a call for anything about how he thinks, and use email for facts. Should send few, numbered questions, each answerable alone, with a date needed by. In the piece, his answers are attributed as 'said in an email'. Should verify his credential rather than repeating how he describes himself, and ask about any conflict of interest.
expectations: Recommends a call for reasoning and email for facts
Sends few numbered questions with a deadline
Attributes written answers as said in an email
